section_title: SST Interneuron Identity: Transcriptomic Subtypes, Connectivity, and Somatostatin Receptor Signaling
thesis: 'SST interneuron' names a marker, not a cell type: the label spans at least a dozen transcriptomic and morpho-electric types with different laminar targets, different output preferences and different state modulation, and the genetic tools used to access them are neither complete nor specific. Every disease claim about 'SST interneurons' is therefore a claim about whichever subset a given marker or driver line reports.
scope_notes: Foundation section. Covers transcriptomic subtypes, connectivity motifs and SSTR1-5 signaling, which later sections need to interpret disease findings.

arg_conflict_cluster_01_conf_01.thesis: Whether Sst interneurons form recurrent Sst→Sst connections: paired recordings in mouse V1 slices reported a lack of Sst-Sst connections in L2/3 and L5, whereas large-scale multipatch recordings in mouse and human neocortex observed Sst-Sst connections in every layer (with Patch-seq confirmation of 5/66 probed pairs). Differences in Cre-line specificity (Sst-IRES-Cre labels some Pvalb-like fast-spiking cells), sampling scale, and detection sensitivity may contribute; SOM-SOM disinhibition during cooperative recruitment (10.1016/j.neuron.2016.02.037) supports the existence of functional Sst-Sst inhibition.
arg_conflict_cluster_01_conf_01.synthesis: Conflict cluster_01_conf_01 (foreground; resolution_status=open). Whether SST cells form recurrent SST->SST connections determines whether the class can disinhibit itself, and the disagreement is a pure measurement-scale/driver-line issue - the template for the whole review. Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): species_region_and_circuit_context.

arg_conflict_cluster_01_conf_05.thesis: Morphological identity of layer 4 SST interneurons: one study reports that L4-targeting SOM+ cells constitute a single non-Martinotti population, whereas paired-recording work finds L4 SST cells to be non-Martinotti in somatosensory cortex but Martinotti-like in visual cortex. The disagreement concerns whether non-Martinotti identity is a property of layer 4 per se or is area-specific.
arg_conflict_cluster_01_conf_05.synthesis: Conflict cluster_01_conf_05 (foreground; resolution_status=open). Whether non-Martinotti identity is a property of layer 4 or of cortical area decides whether laminar disease findings generalise across cortex. Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): species_region_and_circuit_context.

arg_conflict_cluster_01_conf_07.thesis: Interpretation of reporter-based SST cell counts. One study treats reduced eGFP-SST density as a change in the SST population while finding no accompanying death or oxidative-stress signal; the other documents SST-immunonegative tdTomato+ cells in SST-Cre tissue that force exclusion of a whole region from analysis. Together they disagree on whether Cre-reporter density is a valid proxy for SST interneuron number, which is a measurement-validity rather than a biological disagreement.

Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): measurement_modality_and_what_was_counted.

The dimension of disagreement is laminar/subtype-specific target selection (Martinotti vs non-Martinotti L4-targeting SST cells).

The disagreement is on the strength of the canonical VIP->SST disinhibitory motif and whether it is uniform across laminae.

arg_conflict_cluster_01_conf_06.thesis: Functional reach of the VIP->SST disinhibitory motif. Paired recordings find VIP cells inhibit 40-45% of tested SST cells, implying a broadly available disinhibitory pathway, whereas chemogenetic VIP silencing in CA1 produces no significant change in excitatory input processing in superficial pyramidal cells at maximal stimulation. The disagreement is on whether measurable synaptic connectivity translates into disinhibitory control of principal-cell input gain, and it may be reconciled by sublayer and pathway specificity (CA1 superficial vs deep pyramidal cells; neocortex vs hippocampus).

Every disease claim about 'SST interneurons' is therefore a claim about whichever subset a given marker or driver line reports.

subsections.title: From one marker to a dozen types
subsections.job: Establish the taxonomy: transcriptomic types across mouse and human taxonomies, the Martinotti/non-Martinotti axis as an axonal-projection phenotype, Sst Chodl as the long-range nitrergic outlier, and the fact that reported type counts (11-13 groups) are not commensurable across hierarchy levels. Fix the denominator: SST cells are roughly 30% of cortical GABAergic neurons in rodent neocortex but a much smaller share of human striatal interneurons.

subsections.title: Regional variants: hippocampal O-LM/HIPP/bistratified and the striatal SST/NPY/NOS class
subsections.job: Show that the hippocampal and striatal SST populations are not cortical Martinotti cells under another name - different targets, different co-markers, different developmental origin - and that cross-regional vulnerability comparisons in later sections are therefore comparisons between different cells.

subsections.title: Input-output logic: dendritic targeting, VIP-SST disinhibition, SST-PV interactions
subsections.job: Build the circuit motif the disease sections need, and immediately complicate it: connection probabilities differ roughly two-fold across laminae and areas, the canonical VIP->SST motif does not translate uniformly into disinhibitory control of principal-cell input gain, and whether SST cells inhibit each other is disputed.

subsections.title: Somatostatin as a transmitter: processing, release, and SSTR1-5 signalling
subsections.job: Treat the peptide as a signalling molecule in its own right: SSTR1-5 as Gi-coupled receptors, the pharmacological evidence base, and the gaps - no primary measurement of activity-dependent somatostatin release from identified interneurons and no cell-type-resolved SSTR map were retrieved. Flag SST/GABA co-transmission as a widely repeated claim whose primary demonstration was not retrieved. This subsection is the load-bearing setup for the neprilysin axis and for SSTR agonist therapeutics.

subsections.title: What the genetic toolbox actually reports
subsections.job: Close with tool validity: Sst-Cre lines label some PV-like cells and miss some SST cells, with line- and region-dependent error in both directions. State explicitly that this bounds every rodent cell-count phenotype reported in later sections.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Somatostatin peptide release from cortical SST interneurons under physiological firing patterns
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Primary measurements of endogenous SST peptide concentration and spatial spread evoked by natural, rather than optogenetically imposed, activity patterns; available data come from exogenous photo-release, optogenetic bulk stimulation or nanosampling rather than from endogenous release during behaviour
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: The assumption that SST interneurons signal peptidergically under physiological conditions underpins interpretations of somatostatin loss in disease, yet the dose and range of endogenous release are not established

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Cell-type-resolved map of SSTR1-5 expression on identified cortical and hippocampal neuron types
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Primary experimental demonstration - the claim that specific SSTR subtypes are enriched on specific postsynaptic cell types is repeated across reviews, but a systematic cell-type-resolved receptor map validated at protein level was not identified in the retrieved literature
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Risk of false consensus: subtype-selective SSTR pharmacology is proposed as a therapeutic route, and target cell identity determines the predicted circuit effect

evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Direct evidence that GABA and somatostatin are released from the same terminals of an identified SST interneuron onto an identified postsynaptic partner, with separable time courses, rather than inferred from bulk peptide assays and receptor pharmacology
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Whether the peptide and the transmitter are co-packaged and co-released determines whether peptidergic signalling tracks fast inhibition or operates as an independent, activity-threshold-gated channel

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Non-Martinotti SST subtypes outside layer 4 of rodent somatosensory cortex
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Quantified morphological and connectivity data for non-Martinotti SST cells in association cortices, in hippocampus and in human tissue; existing proportions come mainly from mouse S1 and V1
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Reviews generalise the Martinotti/non-Martinotti dichotomy across cortex, but the area-specific results retrieved here suggest the proportions do not transfer

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Negative and null results on SST interneuron integrity
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Dedicated disconfirming literature is sparse: six targeted Europe PMC contradiction queries (logged in search_log) returned only five in-scope papers reporting preserved, unchanged or non-significant SST-related outcomes, and none was an explicit failed replication of a cluster-01 connectivity or receptor claim
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Without published nulls the apparent consistency of SST identity, connectivity and receptor claims may reflect publication bias rather than convergent evidence

unreplicated_claims_to_flag.claim: In mice, sst2 receptors do not mediate anticonvulsant effects and sst4 activation is proconvulsant in an sst2-dependent manner.
SOM+ HIPP and CCK+ HICAP cells inhibit dentate PV basket cells with slow, weak dendritic inhibition that nevertheless sharpens BC spike timing.
Theta-burst/spike-timing protocols induce postsynaptic Ca2+- and T-type VGCC-dependent LTP at SST→CA1 pyramidal synapses.
Sst-Tac1 (non-Martinotti) vs Sst-Reln subtypes show opposite state modulation (synchronized vs running).
Selective SSTR4 agonism augments the M-current specifically in layer V pyramidal neurons and not in interneurons or supragranular pyramidal cells
NDNF-expressing layer 1 interneurons exert layer-specific presynaptic control over SST interneuron output

framing_limits: Human SST subtype data are sparser than mouse; cross-species correspondence of SST subtypes is weak (revisited in sec-conflicts-limitations).
Peptide release and SSTR cell-type mapping are gaps, not established facts - no claim may presuppose them.

certified_evidence_limits.search_coverage: Europe PMC-dominant retrieval. Endpoints actually used: Europe PMC REST search (resultType=core) and fullTextXML, NCBI E-utilities efetch (db=pmc), CrossRef. No other database contributed a comparable share, so coverage claims must be scoped to these sources.
certified_evidence_limits.citation_chasing: None. No backward or forward citation chasing was performed. No section may claim completeness of coverage; write 'no study examining X was retrieved by these searches', never 'no study has examined X'.
certified_evidence_limits.fulltext_shortfall_concentration: The shortfall is concentrated in pre-2000 closed-access postmortem and CSF literature (radioimmunoassay series), which is recorded at abstract level only. Sections whose argument rests on that literature must state the asymmetry in the section body, not only in Methods.
certified_evidence_limits.disconfirming_sweeps: Disconfirming-evidence sweeps were capped per query. Negative-result and conflict coverage is a top-relevance sample, not a census. Report null results as 'reported null results include ...'; never as 'no contradicting evidence exists'. No rate of contradiction may be reported as complete.
certified_evidence_limits.conflict_axis_labels_provisional: Axes were assigned by a documented rule applied to the recorded nature_of_conflict text. Five candidate axes (measurement modality and what was counted; species, region and circuit context; model construct and species transfer; cohort composition, stage and comorbidity; design rigor and statistical unit) were keyword-scored, with the region/species axis down-weighted (0.55) because regional context is named in almost every conflict record, and design rigor up-weighted (1.3) because it is named rarely and only when it is the point. Each conflict carries a primary axis and the full set of axes present, since most of these disagreements are genuinely multi-axis. These tags are a planning classification derived from the conflict text, not a measurement; the writing phase should correct any tag that misreads a conflict, and the atlas figure must state that conflicts can appear in more than one axis row.
certified_evidence_limits.conflict_inventory_caveat: This inventory is the set of disagreements recorded during a search whose disconfirming-evidence sweeps were capped per query. It is a top-relevance sample of the disagreement in this literature, not a census, and no rate of contradiction may be reported as complete.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: Europe PMC-dominant retrieval with no citation chasing (snowball_rounds = 0)
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: No section may claim completeness of coverage. The Methods section states the database scope and the absence of backward/forward citation chasing explicitly. Claims of the form "no study has examined X" are written as "no study examining X was retrieved by these searches", and every such statement in a body section is sourced to a recorded evidence gap rather than asserted.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: Full-text share varies from 77/77 (circuits, cluster_07) to 22/87 (human evidence, cluster_08) because the older postmortem and CSF literature is closed-access
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: Section 9 is the section whose underlying literature is least directly verified. Its thesis is written so that the central synthesis rests on the modern open-access single-nucleus cohorts, with the 1980s radioimmunoassay series treated as a historically important but abstract-level record; the asymmetry is stated in the section itself, not buried in Methods. Section 5 (25/80 full text) carries the same caveat for its historical CSF series.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: Disconfirming-evidence sweeps were capped per query, so negative-result coverage is a top-relevance sample rather than an exhaustive search
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: Null results are reported as "reported null results include ..." and never as "no contradicting evidence exists". Section 11 states that the conflict inventory is a sample of the disagreement in this literature, not a census, and that the true rate of unreplicated or contradicted claims is bounded below by what is recorded here.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: cluster_09's replication ceiling (therapeutics) is met by a single enabling label; 60 of 86 findings are replication_unknown
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: Section 10 is framed as an assessment of translational status, not of efficacy. No therapeutic claim in that section may be described as replicated unless the specific replicating DOI is named, and the section foregrounds that much of the SSTR4 evidence base comes from one closely related research programme.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: Figure comparisons are heterogeneous: no figure_data entry is uniform on all four homogeneity_check fields
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: Every figure specification states the heterogeneity it must display rather than smooth, and the document-level figure rules forbid pooled summaries outright.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: Several prominent mechanistic claims are flagged as false-consensus risks in the evidence record (metabolic load as the cause of SST vulnerability; SST/GABA co-transmission; absolute sparing of striatal interneurons in HD)
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: Each is introduced in prose as a widely repeated claim whose primary demonstration was not retrieved, in sections 3, 2 and 6 respectively, and each is listed in the section 11 open-questions inventory.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.topic: From one marker to a dozen types
suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Establish the taxonomy: transcriptomic types across mouse and human taxonomies, the Martinotti/non-Martinotti axis as an axonal-projection phenotype, Sst Chodl as the long-range nitrergic outlier, and the fact that reported type counts (11-13 groups) are not commensurable across hierarchy levels. Fix the denominator: SST cells are roughly 30% of cortical GABAergic neurons in rodent neocortex but a much smaller share of human striatal interneurons.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.topic: Regional variants: hippocampal O-LM/HIPP/bistratified and the striatal SST/NPY/NOS class
suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Show that the hippocampal and striatal SST populations are not cortical Martinotti cells under another name - different targets, different co-markers, different developmental origin - and that cross-regional vulnerability comparisons in later sections are therefore comparisons between different cells.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.topic: Input-output logic: dendritic targeting, VIP-SST disinhibition, SST-PV interactions
suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Build the circuit motif the disease sections need, and immediately complicate it: connection probabilities differ roughly two-fold across laminae and areas, the canonical VIP->SST motif does not translate uniformly into disinhibitory control of principal-cell input gain, and whether SST cells inhibit each other is disputed.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.topic: Somatostatin as a transmitter: processing, release, and SSTR1-5 signalling
suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Treat the peptide as a signalling molecule in its own right: SSTR1-5 as Gi-coupled receptors, the pharmacological evidence base, and the gaps - no primary measurement of activity-dependent somatostatin release from identified interneurons and no cell-type-resolved SSTR map were retrieved. Flag SST/GABA co-transmission as a widely repeated claim whose primary demonstration was not retrieved. This subsection is the load-bearing setup for the neprilysin axis and for SSTR agonist therapeutics.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.topic: What the genetic toolbox actually reports
suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Close with tool validity: Sst-Cre lines label some PV-like cells and miss some SST cells, with line- and region-dependent error in both directions. State explicitly that this bounds every rodent cell-count phenotype reported in later sections.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_explains_the_discrepancy: Whether Sst interneurons form recurrent Sst→Sst connections: paired recordings in mouse V1 slices reported a lack of Sst-Sst connections in L2/3 and L5, whereas large-scale multipatch recordings in mouse and human neocortex observed Sst-Sst connections in every layer (with Patch-seq confirmation of 5/66 probed pairs). Differences in Cre-line specificity (Sst-IRES-Cre labels some Pvalb-like fast-spiking cells), sampling scale, and detection sensitivity may contribute; SOM-SOM disinhibition during cooperative recruitment (10.1016/j.neuron.2016.02.037) supports the existence of functional Sst-Sst inhibition.

Morphological identity of layer 4 SST interneurons: one study reports that L4-targeting SOM+ cells constitute a single non-Martinotti population, whereas paired-recording work finds L4 SST cells to be non-Martinotti in somatosensory cortex but Martinotti-like in visual cortex. The disagreement concerns whether non-Martinotti identity is a property of layer 4 per se or is area-specific.

Interpretation of reporter-based SST cell counts. One study treats reduced eGFP-SST density as a change in the SST population while finding no accompanying death or oxidative-stress signal; the other documents SST-immunonegative tdTomato+ cells in SST-Cre tissue that force exclusion of a whole region from analysis. Together they disagree on whether Cre-reporter density is a valid proxy for SST interneuron number, which is a measurement-validity rather than a biological disagreement.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Not tied to a named figure comparison or a recorded conflict; group into convergent paragraphs of 5-8 citations each rather than covering sequentially.

curation_notes.assignment_rule: Deterministic cluster->section mapping from gate_scope.json cluster_to_section_assignment, applied to unique (doi, claim_source_sentence) evidence units.
curation_notes.bookend_rule: Sections 01 and 12 are bookends written at Phase 11 and may cite only papers already used in body sections. Each bookend finding is a Phase 2 finding whose DOI also carries a different finding, with a different claim_source_sentence, in a body section - so the paper is already in the body and the two sections quote different sentences.
curation_notes.duplicate_policy: 35 of 844 Phase 2 findings were byte-identical (same DOI and same claim_source_sentence) records of the same observation in two or more clusters. They were merged into the surviving finding object (also_recorded_in_clusters / duplicate_finding_ids_merged) and logged in unassigned_findings.json; none were deleted.
curation_notes.conflict_axis_caveat: AXIS labels on conflicts are rule-derived and provisional (scaffold conflict_coverage.axis_assignment_method). Correct any tag that misreads a conflict.
curation_notes.citation_discipline: Papers in this package come only from Phase 2 outputs. Do not introduce new citations; cite_keys are from the certified citation_key_map and author names only from author_name_table.
